title: Can Conservatives Go Green? | Institute for Family Studies
gist: Teaser of an American Conservative piece (Grace Plath) on a growing conservative environmental movement — e.g., Vita Et Terra and the American Conservation Coalition — that frames more humans as a solution rather than a problem and is attracting young conservatives alienated by left-wing environmental messaging.

insights.claim: A growing conservative environmental movement, including the new nonprofit Vita Et Terra co-founded by Clare Ath, sees more humans as a solution to environmental problems rather than a problem.
insights.speaker: Grace Plath
insights.so_what: A pro-natalist environmentalism decouples climate concern from anti-growth framing; could shift right-of-center policy on conservation.
insights.quote: sees more humans as a solution, not a problem
insights.locator: Clare Ath always loved the outdoors.

insights.claim: The American Conservation Coalition (ACC), led by CEO Danielle Franz, has over 100,000 members and brands itself as 'a new kind of environmental movement' aimed at college students and young professionals.
insights.speaker: Grace Plath
insights.so_what: A sizable right-leaning green constituency could broaden bipartisan support for conservation and energy-transition policies.
insights.quote: a new kind of environmental movement
insights.locator: That message is resonating with young

insights.claim: Young conservatives who don't connect with left-wing environmental messaging still care about the planet, creating an opening for conservative-branded stewardship organizations.
insights.speaker: Grace Plath
insights.so_what: Environmental politics may be less partisan among younger cohorts than headline polarization suggests.
insights.quote: young conservatives who don’t connect with left-wing environmental messaging but still care about the planet
insights.locator: That message is resonating with young
